title: Alljoined-1.6M
description: Alljoined-1.6M is a large-scale EEG dataset capturing neural responses to rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) of natural images from the THINGS database, recorded using a consumer-grade 32-channel EMOTIV FLEX2 system. Twenty healthy adults completed four sessions each, yielding over 1.6 million visual stimulus trials with an interleaved oddball detection task. The dataset was designed to evaluate whether affordable, consumer-grade EEG hardware can support deep learning-based brain-computer interface and semantic decoding research comparable to costly research-grade systems.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 32-channel EMOTIV FLEX2 system (sintered Ag/AgCl gel electrodes, wireless Bluetooth 5.2) at 256 Hz, using an extended 10-20 montage focused on occipital/visual regions, with built-in dual 50/60 Hz notch filtering. Participants viewed a rapid serial visual presentation paradigm (100 ms image, 100 ms blank) drawn from 16,740 THINGS database images, performing an orthogonal oddball detection task (button press for Woody character catch trials, ~6% of sequences) across four sessions of 19 runs each.
